blockers.message: the review record has no `## plan.challenge` section, while roles were active at it
R-ops-1 (Payment call has no timeout and can hang the checkout forever) is high and still open; fix it, or a human accepts the risk or defers it
R-ops-2 (Unbounded retry of a non-idempotent charge can duplicate charges) is high and still open; fix it, or a human accepts the risk or defers it
R-ops-3 (Failed charge attempts are swallowed without any log) is high and still open; fix it, or a human accepts the risk or defers it

findings.recommendation: Pass an explicit `timeout=` (connect and read) to `requests.post`. Without it, when the provider accepts the connection but stops answering, the call blocks indefinitely and the checkout request that called `charge` never returns; the operator sees stuck workers with no error and no log.
findings.title: Payment call has no timeout and can hang the checkout forever

findings.recommendation: Bound the retries (a small maximum, with exponential backoff and jitter instead of a fixed 1 s sleep) and raise once they are exhausted. Retry only transient failures (connection errors, timeouts, 5xx/429) — `raise_for_status` turns a 4xx such as a declined card into an `HTTPError`, which this loop retries forever. Send an idempotency key derived from `order_id` so a retry after a read timeout or a lost response, where the provider already charged, does not charge the customer twice. Today, a provider outage turns every checkout into an infinite loop hammering the provider once a second, and a lost response can charge the same order repeatedly.
findings.title: Unbounded retry of a non-idempotent charge can duplicate charges

findings.recommendation: Log each failed attempt with structured fields (order_id, attempt number, HTTP status or exception type, provider URL — never the request body or credentials), and log/raise an actionable error when retries are exhausted. As written, when the provider rejects or fails every request, nothing is logged and no error surfaces: the operator cannot tell that charges are failing, nor for which orders or why.
findings.title: Failed charge attempts are swallowed without any log

findings.recommendation: Read the provider URL from the environment or the application's configuration (with the production value as deployment configuration, not a code default). The provider endpoint differs between environments; hard-coded, a staging or local run charges the production provider, and switching to a sandbox or a new endpoint requires a new release.
findings.title: Payment provider URL hard-coded instead of read from configuration
